solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Missing the past lots again, sadly (9)

indicatorNotes.sadly: things gone sadly have gone wrong, so the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: Someone mournfully reflecting that a lot is being lost all over again.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leads and 'sadly' ends the clue, so it is easy to read the whole thing as one wistful phrase. 'Sadly' also suits the answer's mood.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the word is a wistful longing for earlier times, which is what missing the past feels like.

entries.clue: Inquiry’s intermittently followed by English healthcare worker (5)

indicatorNotes.intermittently: something done intermittently happens at intervals, so take every other letter
indicatorNotes.followed by: puts the next piece after the first

blocks.note: the even letters of INQUIRYS: N, U, R, S

annotation.surface: An inquiry into the health service that keeps pausing and calling an English nurse.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S counts: the letters are taken from INQUIRY'S, which supplies the final S.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: ward staff who care for patients are the most familiar healthcare workers after doctors.

entries.clue: Bag a portion of chips at Chelsea (7)

indicatorNotes.a portion of: the answer is only part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A request to grab some chips at a Chelsea food stall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bag' reads as a verb, to claim some chips; it is the noun, the thing you carry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is a flat shoulder bag, classically the one schoolchildren carried books in.

entries.clue: Fair game to reject loud transport link (3-6)

indicatorNotes.to reject: throws out the letter for 'loud' from the word before

blocks.note: f = forte, loud in music; FAIR loses it

annotation.surface: A plea that a fair game should get rid of noisy transport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' looks like one phrase meaning a legitimate target; it splits into FAIR and game. F for loud comes from musical notation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an air-bridge is a regular air service connecting two places, a link made by transport.

entries.clue: Butcher opens a gyros café (6,5)

indicatorNotes.Butcher: to butcher something is to mangle it, so the letters are hacked about

annotation.surface: A butcher is launching a café selling gyros, the Greek meat wraps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' reads as the man opening the shop, but it is the verb telling you to mangle the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A British slang term: a greasy spoon is a cheap, basic café serving fried breakfasts.

entries.clue: Unrestricted payments to government cut (3)

indicatorNotes.Unrestricted: with its limits removed: the first and last letters go

blocks.note: TAXES with its outer T and S removed

annotation.surface: Taxes paid without limit to the state are then cut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unrestricted' reads as describing generous payments; it means strip off the boundaries of TAXES.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly in its journalistic sense: budgets and jobs are axed when they are cut.

entries.clue: Famous day school experiencing setback (5)

indicatorNotes.experiencing setback: set back means turned round, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: d = day; it starts the string and ends up last

annotation.surface: A well-known day school going through a bad patch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Day school' looks like one phrase for a non-boarding school; it splits into D and a school, which happens to be Eton, a boarding school.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a noted figure is a well-known, famous one.

entries.clue: Man on board’s topless when the sun goes down (5)

indicatorNotes.topless: in a down answer the top is the first letter, so it goes

blocks.note: a chess piece, a man on the board

annotation.surface: A man on a boat goes shirtless once the sun sets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor on a ship; in crosswords a man can be a chess or draughts piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the time after sunset is the dark part of the day.

entries.clue: Crush Liberal’s support for leaders of terrorist regime (7)

indicatorNotes.support for: in a down answer a support sits underneath, so this piece comes after
indicatorNotes.leaders of: the leading letters of the next words

annotation.surface: A call to crush a Liberal who backs terrorist leaders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' is not L for a party member here but an adjective, as in a liberal helping. The apostrophe-S means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to trample is to crush underfoot.

entries.clue: Given film parts, set off (9)

indicatorNotes.parts: the film splits the other word apart and sits in the gap

blocks.note: E.T., Spielberg's film, goes in after the D

annotation.surface: A cast handed their scripts and sent off to start shooting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' reads as roles in a film; it is the verb, the film parting D from ONATED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bomb that is set off has been detonated.

entries.clue: He’s no longer working on plane, maybe having fixed electrical current (7)

indicatorNotes.having fixed: the tree has the current fixed inside it

blocks.note: a plane is a kind of tree
I is the symbol for current in physics

annotation.surface: An engineer who has quit working on aircraft after fitting the wiring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plane' is the tree, not an aircraft, and 'maybe' flags it as one example. I for current is from electrical formulas.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: someone who has stopped working for good is retired.

entries.clue: Insert court expert once found in European books (7)

indicatorNotes.found in: the one piece is located inside the other

blocks.note: NT = New Testament, the books; the tennis player goes between N and T
Steffi Graf, a former tennis champion

annotation.surface: An instruction to bring a former legal expert into European law books.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court expert' suggests a lawyer; the court is a tennis court, and 'once' marks a retired player, Steffi Graf.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from gardening: to engraft is to insert a shoot into a plant, and more generally to implant.

entries.clue: Unspecified number subtracted from lower number (5)

indicatorNotes.subtracted from: take the one letter away from the word that follows

blocks.note: n is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number
nether = lower; the N comes off its front

annotation.surface: A maths instruction: take some number away from a smaller number.
annotation.walkthrough: The final 'number' is not a quantity but something that numbs: ether is an old anaesthetic.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: a number is anything that numbs, and ether was an early anaesthetic.

entries.clue: This might secure pay if sent out (6,3)

indicatorNotes.out: out as in wrong, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A remark that posting this might guarantee your payment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This might secure pay' reads as one phrase about wages; the definition stops at 'secure', meaning fasten.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: this pin fastens cloth together, so it is something that secures.

entries.clue: Chef liked you, mostly getting cooked game from the US (5,6)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.getting cooked: cooked as in mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A chef's fondness for someone, who is now being cooked, in a game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From the US' qualifies the name: Americans need the extra word for what Britons simply call hockey.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: Americans say field hockey to separate the grass game from ice hockey.

entries.clue: Pass tailless young horse (3)

indicatorNotes.tailless: the last letter, the tail, is cut off

blocks.note: a young male horse; its last letter T goes

annotation.surface: Walking past a young horse with no tail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pass' reads as a verb; it is the noun, the dip between two mountain peaks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from geography: a col is a low mountain pass.

entries.clue: Rubbish instrument Charlie picked up for enthusiast (9)

indicatorNotes.picked up: in a down answer, lifting means reading upwards

blocks.note: the cello is a string instrument
C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet
the whole string ROT + CELLO + C is read upwards

annotation.surface: A poor instrument that Charlie bought for someone who loves them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as bought; in a down clue it tells you to turn the whole string upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone who collects stamps or coins is a keen enthusiast for them.

entries.clue: Show contempt for lab workers? Ultimately adjust perception (11)

indicatorNotes.Ultimately: take the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: to dis is to show disrespect
CERN, the physics laboratory near Geneva

annotation.surface: Sneering at scientists, then telling them to finally change their outlook.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'lab workers' warns that the phrase is not what it seems: a named laboratory and a stock word for workers, read separately.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: discernment is keen perception or judgement.

entries.clue: Recalled musical was regularly staged, covering Romeo’s story (9)

indicatorNotes.Recalled: called back, so the whole thing is read in reverse
indicatorNotes.covering: the two words sit on either side of Romeo's letter

blocks.note: R is Romeo in the NATO alphabet
a show that was staged regularly ran

annotation.surface: A remembered musical, once regularly performed, that contained the Romeo story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evita ran' wraps around R, and 'Recalled' then turns the whole string round, not just the musical.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a narrative is an account of events, a story.

entries.clue: Tenant of facility left hospital guards more worn-out (11)

indicatorNotes.guards: the hospital stands at the front of what follows, guarding it

blocks.note: L = left, placed to the left of the facility
facility = ease, as in doing something with facility
H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: The tenant of some building has left the hospital's security staff even more exhausted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facility' suggests a building; it is the other sense, ease or skill.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: someone holding property on a lease is one kind of tenant.

entries.clue: Material that surfaces when key banks start to press hard (7)

indicatorNotes.banks: the key lies alongside the other pieces, like a bank beside a river
indicatorNotes.start to: take the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: the Alt key on a keyboard

annotation.surface: Something that comes to light when a crucial bank begins to squeeze hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Surfaces' reads as emerging; it is the verb for covering a road. 'Key banks' suggests major lenders, but the key is on a keyboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: this tarry mix is what roads and playgrounds are surfaced with.

entries.clue: Gentleman’s opposite majestic basilica, restored at last (3)

indicatorNotes.at last: take the last letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: last letters of majestiC basilicA restoreD

annotation.surface: Across from a gentleman stands a grand basilica, finally restored.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opposite' looks like a position, facing the basilica; it belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned British word: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, the reverse of a gentleman.

entries.clue: Blade severed rope, releasing ring (7)

indicatorNotes.releasing: letting go of the ring, so that letter drops out

blocks.note: O is ring-shaped; it leaves the rope

annotation.surface: A knife sliced a rope, freeing a ring tied to it.
annotation.walkthrough: The rope is specifically a lasso, and O is the crossword's usual ring.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a cutlass is a short curved sword, the sailor's blade.

entries.clue: Language’s incredible power inspiring individual catching end of demonstration (9)

indicatorNotes.catching: the muse holds the letter inside her name

blocks.note: Erato, one of the Muses, who inspire artists
last letter of demonstratioN, placed inside ERATO

annotation.surface: A language with astonishing force, motivating a person to grasp the end of a lecture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like a container instruction; it describes the individual: a Muse, whose job is to inspire.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Esperanto is the best-known invented international language.

entries.clue: Come back to mind mongrel found beneath tree losing coat (5)

indicatorNotes.found beneath: in a down answer, beneath means after
indicatorNotes.losing coat: a coat is the outside layer, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: TREE without its outer T and E
a cur is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: Memories of a stray dog under a tree that was shedding its bark.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coat' pairs naturally with the dog, but it is the tree that loses its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in one sense: a thought or memory that recurs comes back to mind.

entries.clue: Change top when husband leaves (5)

indicatorNotes.leaves: the letter departs from the word

blocks.note: a halter is a sleeveless top tied at the neck
h = husband; it comes off the front of the top

annotation.surface: A woman switches her top once her husband goes out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a garment, specifically a halter top, and it gets changed in the surface too.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to modify something is to change it.

entries.clue: City gets drug for old age (5)

indicatorNotes.gets: the city receives a new letter
indicatorNotes.for: in exchange for, so the new letter replaces the old one

blocks.note: Ripon, a cathedral city in North Yorkshire
E = ecstasy, which replaces the O

annotation.surface: A city takes up drugs to cope with ageing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old age' reads as one phrase; it splits into O and the definition 'age', a verb. Ripon is a small city in Yorkshire.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: cheese and wine mature, or age, as they grow ready.

entries.clue: The Republican Party stops loan instalment (7)

indicatorNotes.stops: to stop something is to plug it, so the party goes inside

blocks.note: ANC, the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

annotation.surface: The Republicans block a loan payment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Republican Party' reads as one US party; it splits into R and a different party altogether.
annotation.definitionFit: A term from finance: a loan or payment released in stages comes in tranches, French for slices.

entries.clue: Slippery character, old PM loses power (3)

indicatorNotes.loses: the letter is dropped from the name

blocks.note: p = power; it comes off the front of the name

annotation.surface: A former prime minister, a slippery sort, is thrown out of office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slippery character' suggests a devious politician, which fits the PM; it is literally a slimy fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition with a pun: the fish is literally slippery, and a shifty person is called an eel.

entries.clue: Swimmer’s fine withdrawn, I complain (3,4)

indicatorNotes.withdrawn: drawn back, so the letters run the other way

annotation.surface: A swimmer grumbles that their penalty has been cancelled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is not a penalty but OK, and 'withdrawn' turns it round.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-style definition by function: any fish is a swimmer, and this is the ornamental pond fish.

entries.clue: It turns to the left or to the right (5)

indicators: to the left or to the right

indicatorNotes.to the left or to the right: the word reads the same in either direction

blocks.clueFragment: to the left or to the right
blocks.note: a palindrome: the same letters read leftward or rightward

annotation.surface: Something that spins either anticlockwise or clockwise.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes it about direction of spin; it means the direction of reading.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the spinning part of a motor or helicopter is the bit that turns.

entries.clue: Amateur actors moving quietly about (9)

indicatorNotes.moving: the letter changes position within the word

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly; it moves from the front to after LAY
on = about, as in a talk on a topic

annotation.surface: Amateur actors creeping silently around the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moving quietly' reads as tiptoeing; it is an instruction to shift the letter for quietly to a new place in the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone without professional training is an amateur.
